instruments.statusNote: From 1 January 2027 a new 1% defence special income tax is added, while the 2.1% reconstruction surtax falls to 1% and runs to 2047 (FY2026 tax reform outline, 26 Dec 2025). The total surtax stays at 2.1%.

names.official: Income Tax (所得税)

taxes.base: Income of individuals resident in Japan (worldwide, with special rules for non-permanent residents) and Japanese-source income of non-residents.
taxes.payer: Individuals; employers withhold on salaries (源泉徴収).

rate.headline: 5% – 45% in seven brackets (plus a 2.1% surtax)
details: A reconstruction special income tax of 2.1% of the income tax is added in 2013–2037.
The basic deduction is being raised and, from the FY2026 reform, indexed to prices; the filing threshold was raised to about ¥1.78 million as a special measure.

instruments.explanation: The largest national tax together with the consumption tax. Withholding at source collects most of it (about 81% of the FY2025 total); the rest comes from year-end adjustments and self-assessed returns.
exceptions: Capital gains and dividends are mostly taxed separately at flat rates (about 20.315% including local tax).

instruments.statusNote: A defence special corporation tax (see its own core) applies from 1 April 2026 in addition to the corporation tax.

names.official: Corporation Tax (法人税)

taxes.base: Income of domestic corporations (worldwide) and Japanese-source income of foreign corporations.

rate.headline: 23.2% standard; 15% on the first ¥8 million for small companies
details: Companies with capital of ¥100 million or less pay 15% on the first ¥8 million of annual income.
Local corporation tax (10.3% of corporation tax), enterprise tax and inhabitant taxes are added; the effective combined rate is about 30%.

instruments.explanation: The tax on company profits, which produced record revenue in FY2025 on strong corporate earnings.
exceptions: Tax incentives for R&D, wage increases and investment are provided by special tax measures.

names.official: Consumption Tax (消費税, national portion)

taxes.base: Sales of goods and services in Japan and imports (a value-added tax with an invoice system).

rate.headline: 10% total (7.8% national + 2.2% local); 8% reduced rate
details: Reduced rate of 8% (6.24% national + 1.76% local) for food and non-alcoholic drinks (excluding dining out) and newspaper subscriptions.
The 2.2% local consumption tax is collected together with the national tax and paid to prefectures (see the prefectural level).

instruments.explanation: The single biggest source of tax revenue in FY2025, at about 31% of general-account tax revenue.
exceptions: Exempt: land, financial services, medical care, education, housing rent. Small businesses under a turnover threshold have special treatment.

names.official: Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax (相続税・贈与税)

taxes.base: Property acquired by inheritance, bequest or gift above the basic exemptions.

details: Inheritance: basic deduction of ¥30 million plus ¥6 million for each statutory heir.
Gifts: annual basic exemption of ¥1.1 million under calendar-year taxation.

instruments.explanation: One statute covers both inheritance and gift taxes, so the Ministry reports them together.
exceptions: Special rules for family businesses and agricultural land.

instruments.statusNote: Beer-type alcoholic beverages move to a single tax rate on 1 October 2026 under the staged reform of the Liquor Tax Act.

names.official: Liquor Tax (酒税)

taxes.base: Alcoholic beverages by volume and type (per kilolitre).
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on to consumers.

rate.headline: Per-kilolitre rates by type and alcohol content
details: Different rates for beer-type, wine, sake, spirits; the beer, 'happoshu' and 'new genre' rates are being unified on 1 October 2026.

instruments.explanation: A national excise tax on alcohol.
exceptions: Wine and beer-type rates were adjusted in stages in 2020, 2023 and 2026.

instruments.statusNote: Heated-tobacco taxation is being aligned with cigarettes in steps on 1 April and 1 October 2026, and the national rate rises by ¥0.5 per stick in each of 2027, 2028 and 2029 to fund defence.

names.official: National Tobacco Tax (たばこ税) and Special Tobacco Tax (たばこ特別税)

taxes.base: Manufactured tobacco by number of sticks (or weight equivalent).

rate.headline: Fixed yen per 1,000 sticks; prefectural and municipal taxes are added
details: Prefectures and municipalities levy their own tobacco taxes (shown at those levels).

instruments.explanation: An excise tax on tobacco, one of the taxes raised to finance stronger defence capabilities.
exceptions: The special tobacco tax funds the government's past debt of the former Japan National Railways.

instruments.statusNote: The special (provisional) rate of the gasoline tax and local gasoline tax was abolished on 31 December 2025. FY2025 revenue includes nine months at the old rate; later years will be lower.

names.official: Gasoline Tax (揮発油税)

taxes.base: Gasoline by volume when it leaves the refinery or is imported.
taxes.payer: Refiners and importers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: Yen per litre; the special rate ended on 31 Dec 2025
details: The base rates remain; the special rate that had applied 'for the time being' since the 1970s no longer does.
A local gasoline tax is levied together and transferred to local governments.

instruments.explanation: A national fuel excise. Its abolition of the provisional rate removes a large portion of its revenue from 2026.
exceptions: A prefectural diesel delivery tax had a matching provisional rate abolished on 1 April 2026.

names.official: Petroleum and Coal Tax (石油石炭税) including the tax for global warming countermeasures

taxes.base: Crude oil, petroleum products, natural gas and coal on import or extraction, by volume or weight.

rate.headline: Yen per kilolitre or tonne, plus a climate surcharge
details: Rates are per kilolitre of crude oil, per tonne of coal and per tonne of gas; a surcharge on top funds global-warming measures.

instruments.explanation: A tax on fossil-fuel energy at the source.
exceptions: Some uses (e.g. naphtha for petrochemicals) are exempt or refunded.

names.official: Motor Vehicle Tonnage Tax (自動車重量税)

taxes.base: Vehicle weight, paid at vehicle inspection.

rate.headline: Yen per 0.5 tonne, by vehicle type and age
details: Reduced rates for eco-friendly vehicles.

instruments.explanation: A national tax on vehicle weight; part of the revenue is passed to municipalities as a local transfer tax.
exceptions: Older vehicles pay more.

names.official: Customs Duties (関税)

taxes.base: Customs value (or quantity) of imported goods by tariff line and origin.

rate.headline: Tariff schedule; low average, preferential rates under trade agreements
details: Rates are set in the Customs Tariff Law and its schedules; most industrial goods face low or zero duty.
EPAs and FTAs (CPTPP, RCEP, the Japan–US and EU agreements) reduce or eliminate many duties.

instruments.explanation: Duties collected by Japan Customs.
exceptions: Agricultural products such as rice and dairy retain high tariffs.

names.official: Stamp Tax (印紙税)

taxes.base: Documents such as contracts, receipts and negotiable instruments listed in the Act.
taxes.payer: The person who prepares the document.

rate.headline: Fixed amounts by document type and value
details: Paid by affixing revenue stamps or by cash payment.

instruments.explanation: An old tax on documents that still raises about ¥1 trillion a year.
exceptions: Electronic contracts are not subject to stamp tax.

instruments.statusNote: From 2027 the rate falls from 2.1% to 1% and the levy is extended until 2047, alongside a new 1% defence special income tax.

names.official: Special Income Tax for Reconstruction (復興特別所得税)

taxes.base: The amount of income tax (a surtax on income tax).

rate.headline: 2.1% of income tax (2013–2037)
details: Credited to the reconstruction special account rather than the general account.

instruments.explanation: A temporary surtax that finances recovery from the 2011 earthquake. It is excluded from the general-account total used for core sizes.
exceptions: Also applies to withholding tax on interest and dividends.

instruments.statusNote: In force for business years beginning on or after 1 April 2026; first collections fall in FY2026 and FY2027.

names.official: Defence Special Corporation Tax (防衛特別法人税)

taxes.base: The corporation-tax amount above ¥5 million.

rate.headline: 4% of (corporation tax − ¥5 million)
details: Imposed as a surtax to finance stronger defence capabilities; there is no scheduled end date.

instruments.explanation: A new surtax on corporation tax that took effect in 2026.
exceptions: Small companies below the ¥5 million allowance pay nothing.

instruments.statusNote: Takes effect on 1 January 2027 (FY2026 tax reform outline).

names.official: Defence Special Income Tax (防衛特別所得税)

taxes.base: The amount of income tax (a surtax on income tax).

rate.headline: 1% of income tax from 1 January 2027
details: Offset by cutting the reconstruction surtax from 2.1% to 1%, so the combined surtax stays at 2.1% for most taxpayers.

instruments.explanation: A new surtax to finance defence spending, designed not to raise household burdens at first.
exceptions: Details for withholding tax are set in the implementing regulations.

names.official: Social insurance premiums (社会保険料: pension, health, long-term care and employment insurance)

taxes.base: Standard monthly remuneration (and bonuses) of employees; flat premiums for the self-employed.
taxes.payer: Employees and employers (equal shares for employees' schemes); self-employed people pay their own premiums.

rate.headline: Employees' pension 18.3% split equally; health insurance about 10% (varies)
details: Employees' Pension Insurance: 18.3% of standard remuneration, half paid by each side.
Health insurance rates vary by scheme and prefecture (about 10% on average for Kyokai Kenpo); long-term care and employment insurance add further premiums.

instruments.explanation: Premiums, not taxes: they give rights to pensions and care. In FY2023 they totalled ¥80.1 trillion, close to the whole national tax revenue.
exceptions: Rates change annually; child-support levies were added from 2026.

names.official: Prefectural Inhabitant Tax (道府県民税 / 都民税)

taxes.base: Individuals' income (income levy and per-capita levy) and corporations' tax (corporate levy).
taxes.payer: Residents and companies with offices in the prefecture.

rate.headline: 4% income levy (standard) plus per-capita levy
details: Standard rates: prefecture 4% + municipality 6% = 10% of taxable income for individuals.
A corporate income-based levy and a per-capita levy by capital size also apply.

instruments.explanation: The prefecture's share of the resident tax, collected together with the municipal share.
exceptions: Prefectures may vary standard rates slightly by ordinance.

names.official: Enterprise Tax (事業税)

taxes.base: Income of businesses; for large corporations also value added and capital ('pro forma standard taxation').

rate.headline: Income-based rates of about 3.5%–7%; pro forma rates for large firms
details: Rates differ by company size and by type of business; a national 'special corporate enterprise tax' is collected on top and redistributed.

instruments.explanation: A prefectural tax on business activity, deductible for corporation tax.
exceptions: Some primary industries and small individual businesses are exempt.

names.official: Local Consumption Tax (地方消費税)

taxes.base: The same sales and imports as the consumption tax (levied as 22/78 of national consumption tax).
taxes.payer: Consumers; collected with the national tax.

rate.headline: 2.2% of the price (1.76% on reduced-rate goods)
details: Collected by the National Tax Agency (and Customs on imports), then apportioned to prefectures; half of each prefecture's revenue is transferred to its municipalities.

instruments.explanation: The prefectural share of the 10% consumption tax.
exceptions: The figure shown includes the half later transferred to municipalities.

names.official: Automobile Tax (自動車税: environmental performance levy and annual levy)

taxes.base: Ownership of passenger cars (annual, by engine size) and the acquisition price of new registrations (environmental performance levy).

rate.headline: Annual ¥25,000–¥110,000 by engine size; environmental levy 0%–3%
details: Reduced or exempt for electric and low-emission vehicles.

instruments.explanation: The main prefectural vehicle tax.
exceptions: Older vehicles pay a surcharge.

instruments.statusNote: The provisional rate of ¥32.1 per litre was abolished on 1 April 2026, leaving ¥15 per litre; the revenue shown is for FY2024 at the old rate.

names.official: Diesel Delivery Tax (軽油引取税)

taxes.base: Diesel fuel delivered to purchasers.

rate.headline: ¥15 per litre since 1 April 2026 (was ¥32.1)
details: Set as yen per kilolitre in the Local Tax Act.

instruments.explanation: A prefectural fuel tax that funds roads.
exceptions: Exemptions for agriculture and some machinery.

names.official: Real Estate Acquisition Tax (不動産取得税)

taxes.base: Assessed value of land and buildings acquired.

rate.headline: 3% for housing and land; 4% for other buildings
details: Reduced special rates and deductions for housing.

instruments.explanation: A one-time tax on acquiring real estate.
exceptions: Inheritance is not taxed.

names.official: Prefectural Tobacco Tax (道府県たばこ税)

taxes.base: Manufactured tobacco sold in the prefecture.

rate.headline: Fixed yen per 1,000 sticks
details: Levied together with national and municipal tobacco taxes.

instruments.explanation: The prefectural component of Japan's tobacco taxes.
exceptions: Heated tobacco is being aligned with cigarettes in stages.

names.official: Municipal Inhabitant Tax (市町村民税 / 特別区民税)

taxes.base: Individuals' income (income levy and per-capita levy) and corporations' tax (corporate income levy and per-capita levy).
taxes.payer: Residents and companies with offices in the municipality.

rate.headline: 6% income levy (standard) plus per-capita levy
details: Corporate levy: 7.0%–8.4% of corporation tax plus a per-capita amount by capital and staff.

instruments.explanation: The largest municipal tax; individuals' income levy dominates.
exceptions: Tokyo's special wards' corporate inhabitant tax is collected by the metropolis and shared.

names.official: Fixed Assets Tax (固定資産税)

taxes.base: Assessed value of land, buildings and depreciable business assets as of 1 January.

rate.headline: 1.4% of assessed value (standard rate)
details: Reduced assessed values for homes on residential land.
Assessed values are revised every three years.

instruments.explanation: Japan's property tax and a stable source for municipalities.
exceptions: In Tokyo's 23 wards the metropolis collects it.

names.official: City Planning Tax (都市計画税)

taxes.base: Assessed value of land and buildings in urbanisation areas.

rate.headline: Up to 0.3% of assessed value
details: A purpose tax earmarked for urban planning and land-readjustment projects.

instruments.explanation: An earmarked tax paid together with the fixed assets tax in designated areas.
exceptions: Only municipalities with city-planning areas may levy it.

names.official: Municipal Tobacco Tax (市町村たばこ税)

taxes.base: Manufactured tobacco sold in the municipality.

rate.headline: Fixed yen per 1,000 sticks
details: Levied together with national and prefectural tobacco taxes.

instruments.explanation: The municipal component of Japan's tobacco taxes, larger than the prefectural component.
exceptions: Heated tobacco is being aligned with cigarettes in stages.

names.official: Light Motor Vehicle Tax (軽自動車税)

taxes.base: Ownership of light motor vehicles and motorcycles (annual levy), and acquisition of new ones (environmental performance levy).

rate.headline: Annual yen amount by vehicle class (¥10,800 for a passenger kei car)
details: Higher for older vehicles, lower for eco-friendly ones.

instruments.explanation: The municipal counterpart of the prefectural automobile tax.
exceptions: Not levied on small motorised bicycles beyond a nominal amount.
